No confirmed substantive mathematical error in a principal result remains in the examined assessments, although review depth varies and some dependencies remain partly checked. Chapter 8 presents the strongest reservation: a specialist review requests major revision of compressed analytic arguments. In Chapter 6, an apparent polarity error was withdrawn after an overbar lost during PDF extraction was recovered from the typeset source. Subsequent research independently reuses the Chapter 3 proof mechanism and confirms that Connes's rigidity conjecture is false, without independently reproducing Chapter 4's stronger infinite-family result. Among the cited follow-ups, Chapter 7 receives the strongest direct theorem-level corroboration through a stronger hardness theorem. Related equality results in Chapter 8 do not verify the analytic inequality proof. Some follow-ups disclose material AI assistance. We argue that confidence should combine formal checking, human reconstruction, independent mathematical use, and a public record supporting correction of both proofs and reviews.

item.title: Kusner's conjecture on equilateral sets is false
item.dc:creator: Logan R. Chalmers
item.description:
The existence of a 58-point equilateral set in ℓ5^56 is formalised in Lean, using only standard axioms; the source is released on Zenodo.
We disprove Kusner's 1983 conjecture that every equilateral set in $\ell_p^n$ with $2<p<\infty$ has at most $n+1$ points: there exist $58$ points in $\mathbb{R}^{56}$ whose pairwise $\ell_5$ distances are all equal, so the maximum equilateral-set size satisfies $e(\ell_5^{56})\ge58>57$. This is the first equilateral set of more than $n+1$ points in $\ell_p^n$ for any finite $p\ge2$. The construction persists on an open interval of exponents around $5$. The configuration is specified by the unique solution of an explicit polynomial system with rational coefficients in a rational box; existence and uniqueness are proved by exact integer inequalities. The existence of the $58$-point equilateral set in $\ell_5^{56}$ has been formalised in Lean from standard axioms.

item.title: A solution to the inverse generator problem and related questions
item.dc:creator: Emiel Lorist, Martin Meyries, Mark Veraar
item.description:
The proof of the main finite-dimensional matrix construction (Theorem 1.1) was formalized in Lean 4, with AI assistance, and released as an artifact.
We give a negative solution to the inverse generator problem on Hilbert spaces. More precisely, we construct a bounded operator $A$ with dense range on a Hilbert space $H$ that generates a bounded, strongly stable $C_0$-semigroup, while $A^{-1}$ does not generate a $C_0$-semigroup. We also construct an exponentially stable generator $A$ with $0 \in ρ(A)$ such that the inverse semigroup is unbounded and grows at least double logarithmically. For the latter generator, every Cayley transform satisfies the ordinary Kreiss resolvent condition but is neither strongly Kreiss bounded nor power bounded. Moreover, its powers satisfy a doubly logarithmic lower bound. Therefore, the Crank–Nicolson scheme is unstable in operator norm both for every fixed step size over long times and under mesh refinement at any fixed final time. Our counterexamples are deduced from a common finite-dimensional construction. For $α\in(0,1)$, we use explicit bases of $\mathbb C^{2n}$ whose partial-sum projections are uniformly bounded and whose unconditionality constants are comparable to $n^α$. The matrices underlying the counterexamples are then obtained as Schauder multipliers with respect to these bases, using a sequence of eigenvalues whose moduli decay doubly exponentially.

item.title: A fast dynamo with zero topological entropy
item.dc:creator: Lukas Niebel
item.description:
The manuscript's fast-dynamo construction and proofs are formalised in Lean 4, with the formalisation released in a GitHub repository (FastDynamo).
We construct an autonomous Lipschitz fast dynamo on the flat three-torus whose particle flow has zero topological entropy and whose ideal induction equation has no exponential growth. We perform a multiscale construction starting from the Ponomarenko flow. For every sufficiently small positive magnetic diffusivity, the induction operator on $\mathbb{T}^3$ has an eigenvalue with real part bounded below by a positive constant independent of the diffusivity. A corresponding non-zero real-valued magnetic field satisfies an exact exponential growth law in $\mathrm{L}^2$. For the same velocity field, every solution of the ideal problem grows at most linearly in $\mathrm{L}^2$. Moreover, the particle flow and its inverse have Lipschitz constants growing at most linearly in time and thus zero topological entropy. The velocity field is real-valued, divergence-free, differentiable everywhere and smooth away from one circle, but is not $\mathrm{C}^1$.

item.title: A finite forbidden family with superlinear surplus and non-join extremal graphs
item.dc:creator: Chuandong Xu
item.description:
Provides a complete Lean 4 formalization of the main counterexample theorem and its general-p extension in a public GitHub repository.
We give a common counterexample to two product-structure conjectures in extremal graph theory. More precisely, we construct a fixed nonempty finite family $\mathcal L$ with $p(\mathcal L)=2$ such that, for some $c>0$, \[ \operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal L)>t_2(n)+cn^{3/2} \] for every sufficiently large $n$. Nevertheless, at every such order there is an $\mathcal L$-extremal graph whose complement is connected and which therefore admits no decomposition as a join of two nonempty graphs. This superlinear surplus also forces the decomposition family of $\mathcal L$ to contain no forest. The construction uses endpoint-injective repair with a finite obstruction family admitting an exact extremal formula and equality classification.

item.title: Tiling a triangle into a prime number of congruent triangles
item.dc:creator: Michael Beeson, Grigore Roşu
item.description:
All proofs on prime triangle tilings are formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib, largely using Claude, with code released on GitHub.
We prove that if a triangle is cut into $N$ congruent triangles and $N$ is prime, then $N=2$, $N=3$, or $N\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, and every such $N$ occurs. In particular, if $N > 3$ then $N$ is not a prime congruent to $3$ modulo $4$. All the proofs in this paper have been formalized in Lean. The argument divides into cases according to possible shapes of the tiled triangle. Let $α,β,γ$ be the angles of the tile. Prior to this posting, there remained several open shapes. The two most difficult shapes were $(2α,β,α+β)$, the {\em triquadratic} shape, and $(β,β,3α)$, the {\em isosceles-$β$} shape, in which $3α+2β= π$ and $α$ is not a rational multiple of $π$. A previous version of this paper relied on incorrect proofs of those cases, which have been retracted, and are replaced here by correct proofs. For each of those two shapes the number of tiles has the form $N = j^2 N_0$, where $N_0 > 1$ is determined by the shape of the tile and $j$ is a positive integer; so $N$ is prime, or even squarefree, only if $j = 1$. We prove by geometric reasoning that neither shape admits a tiling with $j = 1$, which shows that for both shapes $N$ is never prime, and indeed never squarefree. The shape $(β,β,3α+β)$ (where $3α+ 3β= π$) has been settled by Bonfioli. In this paper, we settle the remaining cases, by number-theoretic arguments based on the area equation. Those proofs rule out $N$ prime, but not $N$ squarefree, and we give examples to show that tilings with squarefree $N$ do sometimes exist.

item.title: The four-dimensional Anderson model: a case study for critical SPDEs
item.dc:creator: Yu Deng, Hao Shen
item.description:
The proof of the main theorem was autoformalized in Lean 4 with outside help, assuming one proposition proved in a companion paper.
We study the weakly coupled elliptic Anderson model with spatial white noise on the four-dimensional torus, which provides a basic example of a critical SPDE requiring renormalization at arbitrarily high orders. With coupling $λ|\log\varepsilon|^{-\frac12}$ where $λ>0$ is sufficiently small, we prove that the Green's function of the corresponding random Schrödinger operator, suitably centered and rescaled, converges to a centered Gaussian random field with explicit covariance. The main difficulty is that, for such critical models, one must expand up to order $|\log\varepsilon|$, while the perturbative expansion contains factorially many pairings and a growing number of renormalization terms. To overcome this, we construct a truncated renormalized parametrix and prove sharp high-order bounds for its remainder. A central ingredient is a multiscale analysis based on a new version of Hepp trees, combined with new estimates for summations over permutations. These estimates reveal a precise balance between logarithmic losses from scale summation and factorial gains from the structure of primitive pairings. The methods developed here are intended as a first step toward a general theory for critical SPDEs with weak couplings.

item.title: Ceci n'est pas une pipe: A semantics of justified reliance for AI systems
item.dc:creator: Jade Alglave, Patrick Cousot
item.description:
Theorem encodings of the justified-reliance semantics are checked in Lean 4.24.0 using only its core library, alongside Z3 checks and an OCaml harness.
An AI agent may keep a successful check in context after an edit has invalidated its evidence. We give a semantics for specifying when a system may rely on a message and act on it. Reliability checks an asserted claim against accepted domain knowledge, sources, and messages in the selected context. Justified reliance additionally checks current evidence, authority, and the proposed world change. Relational component semantics and event traces represent nondeterministic outputs, iteration, and external changes. We characterise when merging claims preserves derivable conclusion classes, then construct the coarsest permitted quotient whose rules preserve the exact statuses of designated concrete claims. Construction is polynomial for unary rules; deciding even one permitted merge is coNP-complete for acyclic binary rules. This applies completeness and strong-preservation methods to the execution of quotiented rules. We also relate transition safeguards to runtime enforcement. Relative to a supplied set of possible worlds, a sound guard accepts an observation only when every matching world passes the checks. Exact acceptance requires observations that distinguish opposite-decision worlds; choosing sufficient services is NP-complete on explicit finite tables. A complete finite passport-renewal instance, Lean theorem encodings, Z3 instance checks, and an OCaml harness exercise the semantics. Domain knowledge, interpretation, source licenses, and policy remain application inputs.
